title: Cameco Closes Deal to Increase Ownership in Cigar Lake Mine
summary: Cameco (TSX: CCO; NYSE: CCJ) today announced that the acquisition of TEPCO Resources Inc.’s 5% participating interest in the Cigar Lake Joint Venture by Cameco and Orano Canada Inc. (Orano) has closed.
body_text: Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, Canada, July 2, 2026 All amounts in Canadian dollars unless specified otherwise. Cameco (TSX: CCO; NYSE: CCJ) today announced that the acquisition of TEPCO Resources Inc.’s 5% participating interest in the Cigar Lake Joint Venture by Cameco and Orano Canada Inc. (Orano) has closed. Cameco’s ownership stake in the Cigar Lake uranium mine in northern Saskatchewan has now increased by 2.871 percentage points to 57.418%, while Orano’s share has risen by 2.129 percentage points to 42.582%. For more information regarding the transaction, please see Cameco’s June 1, 2026 news release announcing the acquisition. Profile Cameco is one of the largest global providers of the uranium fuel needed to power a secure energy future. Our competitive position is based on our controlling ownership of the world’s largest high-grade reserves and low-cost operations, as well as significant investments across the nuclear fuel cycle, including ownership interests in Westinghouse Electric Company and Global Laser Enrichment. Utilities around the world rely on Cameco to provide global nuclear fuel solutions for the generation of safe, reliable, carbon-free nuclear power. Our shares trade on the Toronto and New York stock exchanges. Our head office is in Saskatoon, Saskatchewan, Canada. As used in this news release, the terms we, us, our, the Company and Cameco mean Cameco Corporation and its subsidiaries unless otherwise indicated. The Ins and Outs of Body Image and Eating Disorders
summary: Explore Body image and eating disorders. Learn causes, symptoms, and treatments. Discover social media's impact on mental health.
body_text: Body image and eating disorders hold a significant place in the field of mental health. Their complex interrelationship can lead to profound impacts on an individual's physical and emotional well-being. To grasp the essentials without diving deep: Body Image : It's the perception individuals have about their bodies, which might not align with how their bodies actually appear. Eating Disorders : These are serious mental illnesses that can be influenced by various factors, including but not limited to body image distress. Understanding these concepts is crucial because body dissatisfaction is not only seen in those with eating disorders but also in individuals with conditions like depression and anxiety. Understanding Body Image and Eating Disorders When we talk about body image and eating disorders , it's important to understand the key players involved. Let's break down some of the main disorders that often come up in these discussions. Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD) Body Dysmorphic Disorder is a condition where individuals obsess over perceived flaws in their appearance. These flaws are often minor or nonexistent, but the distress they cause can be overwhelming. People with BDD might engage in repetitive behaviors, like checking mirrors or seeking reassurance, and these actions can interfere with daily life. Anorexia Nervosa Anorexia Nervosa is one of the most well-known eating disorders. It involves an intense fear of gaining weight and a distorted body image. Individuals with anorexia often see themselves as overweight, even when they are dangerously underweight. This disorder can lead to severe health issues due to extreme food restriction and can be life-threatening. Bulimia Nervosa Bulimia Nervosa involves cycles of binge eating followed by purging. People with bulimia may consume large amounts of food and then try to get rid of the calories through vomiting, fasting, or excessive exercise. Like anorexia, bulimia is associated with a preoccupation with body shape and weight, but the behaviors and physical consequences are different. Understanding these disorders is crucial because they highlight the complex relationship between body image and eating disorders. While not everyone with an eating disorder has a distorted body image, negative body image can be a significant risk factor for developing these conditions. Causes and Risk Factors When it comes to body image and eating disorders , understanding the causes and risk factors is essential. Let's explore some of the key influences that can increase the risk of developing these disorders. Social Media Influence Social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok can significantly impact how people perceive their bodies. These platforms often showcase images of "ideal" body types, which are frequently edited or filtered. This constant exposure can lead to body dissatisfaction, especially among young people. Studies have shown that scrolling through these images can make individuals feel worse about their own bodies, feeding into negative body image and possibly leading to disordered eating patterns. Cultural Standards Cultural standards also play a big role in shaping body image. Many societies value thinness, which can pressure individuals to conform to unrealistic body ideals. This pressure is not limited to women; men can also feel the need to achieve a muscular physique. These cultural messages are pervasive and can come from media, family, peers, and even healthcare providers. Over time, these standards can contribute to the development of eating disorders as people strive to meet these often unattainable ideals. Genetic Factors Genetics can also influence the likelihood of developing an eating disorder. Research suggests that if a family member has an eating disorder, there's a higher chance that others in the family might develop one too. This genetic predisposition means that some individuals may be more vulnerable to the environmental and social pressures that can trigger eating disorders. Understanding this genetic link can help in identifying those at higher risk and implementing early interventions . By recognizing these causes and risk factors, we can better understand and address the complex interplay between body image and eating disorders . This knowledge is crucial for developing effective prevention and treatment strategies. Symptoms and Warning Signs Recognizing the symptoms and warning signs of eating disorders is crucial for early intervention and support. Let's explore some key indicators that might suggest someone is struggling with body image or an eating disorder. Body Dissatisfaction Body dissatisfaction is a common symptom and can be an early warning sign of an eating disorder. It involves feeling unhappy with one's body shape, weight, or appearance. This dissatisfaction can lead to behaviors such as excessive dieting or avoidance of social situations involving food. Studies show that about 60% of women and 40% of men experience negative body image, which can contribute to disordered eating. Disordered Eating Disordered eating includes a range of unhealthy eating behaviors that can signal an eating disorder. These might include skipping meals, binge eating, or following extreme diets without medical advice. According to research, warning signs such as making excuses to skip meals, preparing separate meals, or eating in secret are red flags. Disordered eating can escalate into more severe disorders like anorexia nervosa or bulimia nervosa if not addressed. Low Self-Esteem Low self-esteem often accompanies body image issues and eating disorders. Individuals may feel inadequate or unworthy, basing their self-worth on their physical appearance. This mindset can lead to constant self-criticism and a preoccupation with perceived flaws. People with low self-esteem might also frequently check themselves in the mirror or compare themselves to others, further feeding into the cycle of negative body image and disordered eating. Other Warning Signs There are additional warning signs that can indicate an eating disorder. These include: Avoidance of social activities due to body image concerns or eating habits. Excessive exercise to burn calories, even when injured or unwell. Use of laxatives or dietary supplements to lose weight. Frequent trips to the bathroom during or after meals, which might suggest purging behaviors. Knuckle calluses or dental enamel loss from self-induced vomiting. Understanding these symptoms and warning signs is vital for identifying and supporting those who may be struggling with body image and eating disorders . Early recognition can lead to timely intervention and better outcomes for individuals affected by these complex issues. The Impact of Social Media Social media platforms like TikTok and Instagram have become central to how young people perceive their bodies. These platforms are filled with images and videos that often promote unrealistic beauty standards. This constant exposure can lead to harmful effects on body image and contribute to eating disorders. TikTok and Body Image TikTok is a wildly popular app, especially among teenagers. With its short, engaging videos, users are constantly bombarded with content that often highlights slender and toned bodies. Many TikTok trends involve showing off body changes or fitness challenges, which can pressure viewers to conform to these ideals. Research suggests that seeing such content can lead to increased body dissatisfaction. Young people might start comparing themselves to these influencers, feeling inadequate or unhappy with their own bodies. Instagram's Role Instagram is another platform that plays a significant role in shaping body image perceptions. It's a visual platform where users post pictures, often edited or filtered, to present their best selves. This can create a distorted view of reality. A study found that higher usage of Instagram is linked to a greater risk of developing body dysmorphia and eating disorders. The curated nature of Instagram feeds can make users feel that everyone else has a perfect body, leading to feelings of inadequacy and low self-esteem. How Social Media Affects Body Image Perception The way social media impacts body image isn't just about seeing idealized bodies. It's also about the engagement users have with this content. Liking, commenting, and sharing posts can reinforce the importance of appearance and perpetuate the cycle of comparison. Algorithms on these platforms tend to show users more of what they engage with, which means that if someone is interested in fitness or diet content, they will see more of it. This can create an echo chamber that intensifies body image concerns. Moreover, social media influencers often promote products like detox teas or diet supplements, which can encourage unhealthy eating habits. The normalization of these behaviors can make it harder for young people to distinguish between healthy and harmful practices. Moving Forward Understanding the impact of social media on body image is crucial for developing strategies to protect young people. Encouraging critical thinking about the content they consume and promoting diverse body types on these platforms can help counteract some of these negative effects. It's also important for parents, educators, and mental health professionals to have open conversations with young people about the realities of social media and body image. By recognizing the influence of TikTok , Instagram , and other platforms, we can better support individuals in maintaining a healthy and realistic perception of their bodies. This awareness is a key step in preventing the development of eating disorders and promoting positive body image. Prevention and Treatment Strategies Addressing body image and eating disorders early can make a big difference. Let's explore some effective strategies for prevention and treatment. Early Intervention Catching issues early is crucial. When signs of body dissatisfaction or disordered eating appear, it's important to act quickly. Schools, parents, and healthcare providers can play a key role by watching for warning signs like frequent dieting or excessive body checking. Early conversations about body positivity and healthy habits can help prevent more serious problems later on. Therapy Therapy is a powerful tool in treating eating disorders and improving body image. Cognitive-behavioral therapy (CBT) is particularly effective. It helps individuals challenge negative thoughts about their bodies and develop healthier patterns of thinking and behavior. Gratitude-based interventions are also gaining traction. These involve practices like gratitude journals, which encourage people to appreciate their bodies for what they can do, rather than how they look. Support Groups Support groups offer a safe space for sharing experiences and learning from others. They can be a lifeline for those struggling with eating disorders. Groups like The Body Project use cognitive dissonance exercises to help participants actively challenge the thin ideal. Joining a support group can also provide a sense of community and reduce feelings of isolation. Self-Help Strategies There are also several self-help strategies that can support professional treatment: Body Gratitude Journal : Writing daily about positive aspects of one's body can shift focus from appearance to appreciation. Social Media Detox : Cleaning up social media feeds to remove triggering content and following body-positive accounts can improve self-perception. Buy Clothes That Fit : Wearing clothes that fit well now, rather than waiting for a "goal weight," can boost confidence. Challenge Avoidance : Gradually exposing oneself to situations that trigger body anxiety can reduce fear over time. These strategies, combined with professional support, can help individuals develop a healthier relationship with their bodies and reduce the risk of developing eating disorders. By focusing on early intervention, therapy, and community support, we can create a more supportive environment for those struggling with body image issues. Next, we'll dive into some frequently asked questions about body image and eating disorders to further clarify this complex topic. Frequently Asked Questions about Body Image and Eating Disorders Is there a link between body dysmorphia and eating disorders? Yes, there is a connection between body dysmorphic disorder (BDD) and eating disorders. BDD involves an obsessive focus on perceived flaws in one's appearance, which can overlap with the body image concerns seen in eating disorders like anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa. People with BDD may engage in repetitive behaviors such as excessive mirror checking or seeking reassurance, similar to those with eating disorders who may engage in frequent dieting or body checking. However, it's important to note that BDD can exist independently of eating disorders, with individuals fixating on features other than weight, like skin or facial features. What are the disorders related to body image? Several mental health problems are closely linked to body image issues. Eating disorders such as anorexia nervosa and bulimia nervosa prominently feature distorted body image and a preoccupation with weight and shape. Body dysmorphic disorder is another condition where individuals obsess over perceived physical imperfections. Additionally, muscle dysmorphia , often seen in males, involves an obsession with not being muscular enough. These disorders can significantly impact mental health, leading to anxiety, depression, and low self-esteem. What eating disorder does not involve body image? Avoidant/Restrictive Food Intake Disorder (ARFID) is an eating disorder that typically does not involve concerns about body image or weight. Unlike anorexia or bulimia, individuals with ARFID avoid certain foods due to sensory issues, fear of adverse consequences like choking, or a lack of interest in eating. This disorder can lead to nutritional deficiencies and weight loss but is not driven by body image concerns. Understanding ARFID is crucial, as it highlights that not all eating disorders are rooted in body dissatisfaction. By exploring these questions, we gain a clearer understanding of the complex relationship between body image and eating disorders , as well as the diversity of disorders related to body image concerns . Conclusion At MentalHappy, we understand that body image and eating disorders are complex challenges affecting many people. Our mission is to make mental health support more accessible and inclusive for everyone, regardless of their background or financial situation. We offer a digital health platform that connects people with the support they need. By providing expert-led support groups and free mental health resources, we aim to create a safe space for individuals to discuss their struggles and find community care. Our platform is designed with HIPAA-compliant privacy settings and user-friendly tools, making it easy for therapists and facilitators to manage support groups effectively. One of MentalHappy's unique features is our AI-driven health assessments. These assessments help personalize mental health support, ensuring that each user receives care custom to their specific needs. Available on both iOS and Android, our platform ensures that support is just a tap away, making it accessible to all users. By addressing the shortage of mental health professionals, MentalHappy strives to make mental health care scalable and reachable. We believe that by fostering a supportive community, we can help individuals build resilience, improve their well-being, and steer the challenges of body image and eating disorders. Join us on this journey towards a healthier and happier life. Explore our resources and learn more about MentalHappy today. Together, we can make a difference in mental health support and accessibility.

title: Affiliations may aid with homebuying
summary: Discover mortgage programs for medical professionals, attorneys, veterans, Native Americans, rural homebuyers and employees with special benefits.
body_text: Affiliations may aid with homebuying Programs based on your profession, heritage or employer can assist potential buyers in accessing homeownership 4 min read KEY POINTS Specialized programs: Various mortgage programs offer benefits based on profession, heritage, or employer, helping offset homebuying costs. Examples: Programs for medical professionals, lawyers, military members and rural residents provide unique financial advantages. Employer benefits: Some companies offer discounts on closing costs and other fees through partnerships with mortgage companies. Think you can’t afford a home? A number of mortgage programs based on your affiliations can help offset the cost of purchasing a home, making home ownership a closer dream than you might think. “We’re starting to see more homebuyers use incentives available through specialty programs that can help ease the financial burden of buying a home in the current climate,” said Julie Haddock , mortgage market leader for Bank of Oklahoma. “With people not having a lot of disposable cash, these programs can provide more options for borrowers.” Know what’s available Whether it’s a program based on your profession, your heritage or even the company you work for, it’s worth digging into all options available when hoping to purchase a home, said Bill North , North Texas market leader for BOK Financial Mortgage®. “All homebuyers have unique financial goals, so exploring various options for financing a mortgage ensures they find a loan that best fits their needs, whether it's lower monthly payments, shorter loan terms, or specific features like adjustable rates,” said North. For example, individuals who pursue advanced degrees may run into challenges with purchasing a home right out of school. With the high cost of medical and law school, these professionals often have a significant amount of student loan debt that can hurt their chances of qualifying for a conventional loan because of a higher debt-to-income ratio. Specialized programs unique to certain industries may help those with advanced degrees with downpayment assistance, flexibility on debt-to-income ratios and special consideration for student loan debt. Learn more about the specialized programs: Advanced Medical Professional program benefits MDs, DOs, DPs, DDSs, DMDs, medical residents, medical fellows, DNAPs, CRNAs and more. Advanced Professional Services program supports practicing lawyers with either a J.D. or Esq. designation. U.S. Department of Agriculture Loans . Those living in rural areas may benefit from mortgage loans backed by the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA). Designed for rural homebuyers, these loans offer zero down payment options and competitive interest rates for qualifying rural and farm properties. Members of the military . If you or your spouse has served or is currently serving in the United States military, there may be a program that is right for you. The Military Home Loan Program, backed by the Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) offers military members significant cost savings for home purchases, including no down payments and competitive interest rates. BOK Financial®, Bank of Texas, Bank of Oklahoma and Bank of Albuquerque also offer special discounts through an annual Veteran Appreciation Program, such as waiving the appraisal fee on VA loans around Veterans Day. Section 184 Indian Home Loan Guarantee Program . Members of a federally-recognized tribe may be eligible for the Section 184 loan program backed by HUD’s Office of Native American Programs (ONAP). This program is specifically designed for American Indian and Alaska Native families, Alaska villages, tribes or tribally designated housing entities. The benefits of this kind of loan program include lower down payment requirements and flexible underwriting for qualifying lenders. Company benefits . Some businesses align with a mortgage company or home builder to offer discounts on things like closing costs. Check with your HR department to see if any discounts are available to you just because you’re an employee. “Your company’s benefits office is a good place to research any potential affiliations available to employees,” North said. “For instance, a number of employers are part of the BOK Financial ‘Financial Benefits’ program in which all employees and their extended family members can receive up to $2,000 lender credit on their home purchase or refinance.” What to do if you qualify North said it’s important to talk to your lender to see if you qualify for one of these programs and to confirm the details and ensure you understand the requirements. “Consult with a mortgage advisor who specializes in these types of loans to get personalized service and advice,” he said. “Since each program has specific eligibility criteria based on factors like income, credit score, military service, geographical boundaries, profession or tribal affiliation, these programs might have more complex application processes or additional documentation requirements.” Topics Home Buying and Major Purchases

title: Code Story: Insights from Startup Tech Leaders with Mezmo's Tucker Callaway
summary: Code Story: Insights from Startup Tech Leaders with Mezmo's Tucker Callaway
body_text: Tucker Callaway grew up in Alamo, California, in the Easy Bay Area. And has returned to that area to raise his family – 25-30 minutes outside of the San Francisco area. He studied computer science at Cal, but eventually moved into sales engineering – and then sales. But outside of tech, he is married with 2 kids – one in college, and one in the latter years of high school. There is lots of change going on his family’s life right now, but Tucker finds time to do woodworking and build his own cabinets. Ten years ago, a couple of co-founders built a solution to make log management easier for developers. Tucker joined that company in the past, and observed the dynamics of the industry and the company. They all decided that to take the business of the next level, they needed to change the physics of observability. This is the creation story of Mezmo . ‍

Inertización: El escudo invisible que protege los almacenes de la cadena de suministro
summary: La mayoría de sistemas contra incendios actúan cuando ya hay llamas. La inertización actúa antes. Descubre cómo y por qué importa en logística.
body_text: Sign in Welcome! Log into your account Forgot your password? Get help Password recovery Recover your password A password will be e-mailed to you. Inertización: El escudo invisible que protege los almacenes de la cadena de suministro Un incendio en un centro de distribución no solo pone en riesgo la instalación: puede paralizar toda una cadena de suministro. Te contamos cómo la inertización se ha convertido en una estrategia clave para blindar almacenes automatizados, cámaras de frío y centros logísticos antes de que el fuego llegue a existir. Conocimiento Industria 24/07/2026 Un almacén moderno concentra en pocos metros cuadrados mercancía de alto valor, instalaciones automatizadas y, en muchos casos, productos sensibles al calor o a la humedad. Cuando ese almacén forma parte de una cadena de suministro ajustada, con flujos de entrada y salida constantes, un incendio no solo supone pérdidas materiales: implica retrasos en pedidos, rupturas de stock y un impacto que se propaga a proveedores y clientes. Por eso, en logística, prevenir pesa tanto o más que apagar. El fuego necesita tres ingredientes para existir: combustible, calor y oxígeno. La mayoría de sistemas contra incendios actúan cuando las llamas ya han aparecido, conteniéndolas o extinguiéndolas. La inertización, en cambio, elimina uno de esos tres ingredientes de forma preventiva: reduce el oxígeno disponible en el almacén antes de que exista ningún fuego que combatir. Esta es la razón por la que cada vez más operadores logísticos, 3PL y fabricantes con almacenes propios la están incorporando a sus instalaciones de mayor riesgo o mayor valor. ¿Qué es la inertización? Aplicada al almacén, la inertización consiste en sustituir parte del oxígeno del aire por un gas inerte (normalmente nitrógeno, aunque también dióxido de carbono o argón) hasta crear una atmósfera en la que la combustión resulta prácticamente imposible. El aire contiene alrededor de un 21% de oxígeno; no hace falta eliminarlo por completo, sino bajarlo por debajo de un umbral crítico conocido como concentración límite de oxígeno (LOC), que varía según el tipo de mercancía almacenada, el gas empleado y las condiciones de temperatura y presión de cada nave. Este matiz es especialmente relevante en la cadena de suministro, porque cada almacén guarda productos distintos: no es lo mismo inertizar una nave de racks metálicos con mercancía general que una cámara de congelación farmacéutica o un silo de materia prima a granel. El nivel de oxígeno objetivo, y por tanto el diseño del sistema, se calcula a partir de un análisis de riesgo específico para cada instalación. Además de prevenir incendios, mantener el oxígeno bajo control tiene un efecto secundario muy valorado en logística: ralentiza la oxidación y el deterioro de los productos almacenados. Por eso la inertización resulta especialmente útil en almacenes que gestionan mercancía sensible (alimentos, productos farmacéuticos, componentes electrónicos) donde alargar la vida útil durante el almacenamiento y el tránsito es tan importante como evitar un siniestro. ¿En qué tipo de instalaciones logísticas tiene más sentido implementarla? Sobre todo en almacenes automatizados de gran altura, donde los pasillos estrechos y los sistemas de almacenamiento por compactación dificultan tanto la detección temprana como las labores de extinción; en cámaras de refrigeración y túneles de congelación, entornos muy herméticos donde el fuego puede propagarse de forma más agresiva; y en centros de distribución que almacenan productos inflamables, polvos combustibles o mercancía de alto valor para la cadena de suministro. Sistema de inertización dentro de la cadena de suministro En el entorno del almacén, un sistema de inertización se apoya normalmente en tres piezas: generadores de nitrógeno, sensores que miden de forma continua la concentración de oxígeno, y un sistema de control automatizado que ajusta la inyección de gas para mantener la atmósfera dentro de los niveles de seguridad establecidos. La técnica más habitual en instalaciones logísticas es la purga, que inyecta gas inerte en la nave o depósito para desplazar o diluir el oxígeno presente, y que admite distintas variantes según cómo se gestione esa sustitución: Por dilución : el gas inerte se introduce y se va mezclando con el aire existente hasta reducir progresivamente el oxígeno, una opción sencilla para espacios de geometría irregular. Por desplazamiento : el gas empuja el aire hacia el exterior sin mezclarse apenas con él, lo que suele requerir menos volumen de gas para un mismo resultado. Por presión : el gas se inyecta a presión para acelerar la mezcla y la salida del oxígeno, en instalaciones preparadas para soportar esas variaciones. Por vacío : primero se extrae el aire del recinto y después se llena con gas inerte, lo que permite alcanzar niveles muy bajos de oxígeno con menor consumo de gas, aunque exige equipos capaces de trabajar a baja presión. Junto a la purga, algunos almacenes recurren al blanketing, una capa de gas inerte que cubre el producto almacenado para aislarlo del oxígeno y la humedad, cuando lo que se busca es proteger mercancía concreta más que el volumen completo de la nave. Dos ejemplos ilustran cómo se traduce esto en la cadena de suministro real. El almacén automatizado autoportante de Takeda en Polonia, de 32,5 metros de altura y destinado a productos farmacéuticos, incorpora un sistema de inertización que mantiene el oxígeno por debajo del 15% mediante inyección de nitrógeno, combinado con control de temperatura y humedad, racks de doble profundidad y manejo automatizado de más de 6.500 tarimas. Por su parte, Frigo Logistics, operador 3PL especializado en productos congelados, equipará su nuevo centro de distribución en Polonia con un sistema de inertización pensado para reforzar la protección contra incendios en un entorno de temperaturas bajo cero y alta densidad de almacenamiento. Para una cadena de suministro, incorporar la inertización no significa renunciar a los sistemas tradicionales de detección y extinción, sino sumarles una capa previa de seguridad: una que actúa antes de que el riesgo llegue a materializarse y, con ello, antes de que un incendio pueda convertirse en una interrupción operativa. Relacionado Maria Saucedo María es una periodista experimentada que combina su formación en letras con una visión estratégica de la logística, creando contenido inspirador e informativo para nuestro blog. title: Claude Opus 5 Release Date: What We Know So Far
summary: Claude Opus 5 has not officially launched. Here is what the Honeycomb leak revealed, which Claude models are available now, and what it means for builders.
body_text: Update (July 27, 2026): Claude Opus 5 officially launched on July 24. For the full breakdown of benchmarks, pricing, and what it means for builders, read our launch coverage . Claude Opus 5 launched on July 24, 2026. It is priced at $5 per million input tokens and $25 per million output tokens, the same as Opus 4.8, and is available on the API as claude-opus-5. It is the new default model on Claude Max and the strongest model on Claude Pro. Before the official announcement, the model had one of the more visible pre-launch trails in recent AI history. A codename, two Cursor sightings, and deployment tracker activity all preceded the launch by weeks. Here is how it unfolded. What Is Claude Opus 5? Claude Opus 5 is the latest model in Anthropic's Opus tier, the company's premium line for complex reasoning, coding, and autonomous agent work. It replaced Claude Opus 4.8 (released May 28, 2026) as the Opus flagship. Anthropic's model lineup breaks into distinct tiers. At the top sits the Mythos class, which includes Claude Fable 5 (launched June 9, 2026) and the restricted Claude Mythos 5. Below that is the Opus tier, now led by Opus 5. Then comes Sonnet 5 (June 30, 2026), Anthropic's high-value workhorse, followed by Haiku 4.5 for lightweight, high-volume tasks. Opus 5 slots exactly where pre-launch speculation placed it: between the Mythos tier and Opus 4.8, offering stronger performance than 4.8 at a more accessible price point than Fable 5's $10/$50 per million tokens. How the Launch Unfolded The Honeycomb leak (July 8) On July 8-9, a model called "Claude Honeycomb EAP" appeared inside Cursor's model picker and was pulled within hours. It was a real listing in a shipping product, seen by multiple people and reported by The New Stack before it disappeared. The listing showed a 1M-token context window, an "extra high effort" reasoning mode (a step above the "high" default on Opus 4.8), per-turn controls with safety fallbacks that route to Opus 4.8, and placement alongside other frontier models in Cursor's picker. Two things stood out. The fallback chain stepping down to Opus 4.8 implies Honeycomb sits above 4.8 in capability. Fallbacks conventionally step down, not up. And Cursor has been a reliable pre-launch venue before. A "claude-sonnet-5" identifier surfaced in Google Vertex AI logs before Sonnet 5 launched, following the same pattern. The listing did not include pricing, benchmarks, an official name, or a release date. "Honeycomb" was a codename. Deployment signals (July 23-24) On July 23, deployment trackers reported Opus 5 preparations and described the model as "rolling out across providers." Some users on X claimed they were served improved responses under the Opus 4.8 label . On July 24, a Cursor error dialog surfaced showing the string claude-opus-5-thinking-high, the first appearance of the literal "claude-opus-5" name in a shipping product. Official launch (July 24) Hours after the Cursor string surfaced, Anthropic published the official announcement. Opus 5 scored 43.3% on Frontier-Bench v0.1 (more than double Opus 4.8's 21.1%) and led on most major evaluations. Anthropic described it as approaching Fable 5 intelligence at half the price. What Claude Models Are Available Right Now Claude Fable 5 is Anthropic's most capable publicly available model. It excels at the hardest autonomous tasks: long-running code migrations, complex multi-step research, and anything where getting it right on the first pass saves significant time and money. It costs $10/$50 per million input/output tokens and requires 30-day data retention. Think of this as the specialist you bring in for the toughest jobs. Claude Opus 5 is the new Opus flagship and the model most builders should default to for complex work. It approaches Fable 5 on most benchmarks at half the token cost ($5/$25 per million tokens), with no data retention requirements. It is the default on Claude Max, the strongest model on Claude Pro, and available on Emergent. For most professional work, Opus 5 is where quality and cost find the best balance. Claude Opus 4.8 remains available at the same $5/$25 pricing and continues to serve as the fallback model when Opus 5's safety classifiers flag a request. It supports zero data retention. For builders already using Opus 4.8, Opus 5 is a direct upgrade at the same price. Claude Sonnet 5 is the value pick that has been closing the gap fast. At $3/$15 per million tokens (with introductory pricing of $2/$10 through August 31, 2026), it delivers performance close to Opus 4.8 on many tasks. It is the default model on Claude's free and Pro plans and the best starting point for most everyday work. Claude Haiku 4.5 is the speed and budget option at $1/$5 per million tokens. It handles simple classification, extraction, and high-volume tasks where cost matters more than depth. For most builders, the practical strategy is straightforward: start with Sonnet 5 for everyday work, step up to Opus 5 when accuracy on hard tasks matters, and reserve Fable 5 for the work where failure costs more than the token premium. What This Means If You Build Without Code Opus 5 is a meaningful upgrade over Opus 4.8 for the work AI app-building platforms handle behind the scenes: code generation, multi-step logic, backend reliability, and handling complex app requirements. It delivers those improvements at the same price as Opus 4.8, so the cost of building does not go up. The current model lineup is the strongest it has ever been. Sonnet 5 alone outperforms what was available at the Opus tier just six months ago, and Opus 5 now approaches Fable 5 on most benchmarks at half the cost. On Emergent, Opus 5, Sonnet 5, Fable 5, and all other major models are already available to build with. Stay tuned to Emergent News for more on AI tools, launches, and what they mean for builders.

title: New technology helps screen SC firefighters for pre-cancer
body_text: Anderson County, SC firefighters were offered esophageal pre-cancer screenings using the EsoGuard DNA test, at an event organized by Honea Path Fire Chief and physician Jimmy Smith. The screening involves swallowing a balloon-equipped capsule to collect esophageal cells, a process taking about five minutes. Firefighters have a 62% higher risk of esophageal cancer due to toxic materials in modern building materials. Anderson City Fire Chief Charlie King emphasized the importance of early detection. Smith noted that early diagnosis and treatment can prevent the progression to fatal cancer. The screenings are also recommended for individuals with risk factors, such as family history. See the news story: https://abc7.com/post/esoguard-test-helps-early-detection-of-esophageal-cancer/14785949/

title: SRX Global Board of Directors Authorizes Stock Repurchase Plan of Up to 10 Million Shares or Up to 50% of its Shares Outstanding

The Company is not obligated to repurchase any particular number of shares or any shares in any specific time period and the program may be modified, suspended, or discontinued at any time. title: From Complexity to Clarity: Rethinking Fiduciary Oversight
summary: Fiduciary responsibility doesn’t have to be unclear. Learn how structure helps employers manage oversight with more confidence.
body_text: Most employers understand they have fiduciary responsibility tied to their retirement plan. What’s less clear is how that responsibility actually plays out day to day. It’s easy to assume that working with experienced providers means the details are covered, but even with strong partners in place, the responsibility still sits with the employer. That’s where uncertainty can arise. When Fiduciary Responsibility Becomes Unclear Fiduciary responsibility shows up in small, ongoing decisions across investments, administration, and compliance. In many organizations, those decisions involve multiple people and vendors. Over time, questions may come up regarding who is accountable for decisions, if documentation is being done correctly, and if one provider is being relied on too much. Without clear answers, teams tend to slow down, and what should be routine starts taking more coordination than expected. The Impact of Uncertainty Uncertainty affects how the retirement plan operates. When roles aren’t clearly defined, decisions take longer, oversight becomes reactive, and internal teams spend more time interpreting responsibility than executing it. Over time, this extra effort adds up. Why Clarity Matters in Fiduciary Responsibility Clear fiduciary structure makes responsibility easier to manage. When roles are defined and supported by a consistent framework, teams don’t have to guess or interpret as much. They know where decisions sit and how they should be handled. That kind of clarity can change how a plan is managed day to day. Rethinking How Responsibility Is Organized Traditional plan structures often rely on a mix of providers, each handling a specific piece of the puzzle. That approach can leave employers in the middle, coordinating inputs and connecting the dots. A more structured model brings those responsibilities together, so they operate as part of the same system, rather than separate efforts. How a Pooled Employer Plan Helps Bring Structure A pooled employer plan (PEP) organizes fiduciary responsibilities within a defined framework. Instead of spreading accountability across disconnected providers, the structure is designed to align roles more clearly. That doesn’t eliminate the employer’s role, but it provides more support around how that role is carried out. The CBIZ Approach to Fiduciary Oversight With the CBIZ Retirement Advantage PEP, fiduciary oversight is built into the design of the plan. Dedicated specialists take on defined responsibilities, helping create a clearer governance model for participating employers. For many organizations, that shift makes it easier to move forward with decisions and maintain consistency in how oversight is handled. Connect with our team to see how the CBIZ Retirement Advantage PEP can help organizations adapt to expanding governance expectations and turn complexity into clarity. title: Introducing Infracost Agents: Find Cloud Waste, Fix It in Code
summary: Infracost Agents scans your cloud estate, investigates waste, and drives fixes through PRs, tickets, and AI coding assistants. Now in private beta.
body_text: One of our design partners was walking through findings surfaced by the new Infracost Idle & Unused Resources agent when she spotted something unexpected: two orphaned load balancers in an account that had just been cleaned up. She clicked the link in the finding, confirmed the resources were still running in AWS and wasting money every day. The agent went beyond just flagging the resources as idle. In it's investigation it identified that the Terraform modules managing these resources had been removed from the codebase, but the live infrastructure was never actually destroyed. "I actually thought everything was removed," she said. "The team must have missed some cleanups." Simple human errors compound — quietly, on your bill, every month. This is the gap that Infracost Agents is built to close. Find issues across your entire cloud estate. Map them to code. Investigate them. Fix them. Reports aren't remediation Cloud cost tools are good at finding problems. They surface dashboards, flag anomalies, and generate reports that tell you exactly where money is being wasted. What they don't do is investigate or fix anything. The finding sits in a list. Someone has to investigate it, trace it back to the right codebase, figure out who owns it, open a PR, get it reviewed, and get it merged. For a FinOps team managing thousands of resources across dozens of accounts, that is not a workflow — it is a backlog that grows faster than anyone can drain it. Infracost Agents is different. It doesn't just find issues in your cloud environment — it traces them back to infrastructure code, investigates them, and drives remediation through the workflows your engineering team already uses: pull requests, tickets, and AI coding assistants. The fix happens where it belongs, in code, so your IaC stays the source of truth and drift doesn't compound. That includes resources that were never in IaC to begin with. ClickOps resources — provisioned directly in the console, outside your Terraform or AWS CDK — have historically been invisible to Infracost. Agents surfaces them too. When it can't trace a resource back to code, it still raises the finding so you can decide how to handle remediation. How it works Agents run scheduled checks against your cloud environment and billing data. When a check detects something wrong — an idle resource, a tagging violation, an anomalous cost spike — it triggers an investigation. The investigation is where the work happens: the agent traces the resource to its IaC, infers ownership, enriches the signal with usage and billing context, and produces a finding with the tasks needed to resolve it. From there, you choose how to act. Have the agent open a PR to fix the issue directly in code — no manual changes, no drift. Route it to your engineering backlog as a Jira or Linear ticket, pre-populated with the agent's investigation. Or hand off its findings to your AI coding assistant so you or a developer on your team can collaborate on a fix. Every decision you make teaches the agent. Dismiss a finding because that idle load balancer is tied to a roadmap project that isn't live yet? The agent records that context and won't surface it again until something changes. Over time, the agents get smarter about your environment, your policies, and your team's intent. The first three agents Infracost Agents launches in private beta with three agents: Idle and Unused Resources monitors your cloud estate for resources consuming spend without delivering value — idle EC2 instances, unattached volumes, load balancers with no traffic, clusters with no workloads. It also surfaces orphaned resources that have been removed from code but never destroyed in the cloud. For each finding, it traces the resource to its IaC and opens a removal PR when you're ready. Tagging enforces your tag policies at scale. It scans both IaC-managed and manually created resources, identifies violations, and opens PRs to fix them in code. For resources outside IaC, it flags them explicitly so you know what's drifted from policy. Cost Anomaly Detection ingests anomalies from AWS and thoroughly investigates them — correlating spikes to application and infrastructure changes, identifying the likely root cause, and surfacing the context your team needs to act before the cost compounds. These are the first three. More agents are in development, covering areas like Kubernetes rightsizing, AI cost optimization, and compute right-sizing. Private beta gives you a seat at the table as we build them. What private beta means Infracost Agents is in active development. Private beta customers get hands-on access to the product, direct input into roadmap priorities, and a dedicated channel with the Infracost team. We're looking for engineering and FinOps teams who are serious about reducing cloud waste and willing to help shape what this becomes. If that's you, join the waitlist. We'll reach out when Infracost Agents is ready for your environment. Join the waitlist → Already an Infracost customer? Contact your account team to discuss private beta eligibility.

title: Your Face Closes the Deal Before You Say Anything
summary: What a professional headshot photographer actually delivers, what a good headshot costs you to skip, and how to book quality headshots at scale.
body_text: The Tenth of a Second That Follows You Everywhere Someone lands on your LinkedIn profile, your team page, or your speaker bio. Their brain has already decided whether you look competent and trustworthy, and it happened faster than they can consciously register. Princeton psychologists Janine Willis and Alexander Todorov found that people form those judgments after just a tenth of a second of looking at a face , and that more time to study the face only made them more confident, not more accurate. Trust was among the judgments viewers formed fastest. In other words, the photo is doing the talking, and it never stops. That is the case for hiring a professional headshot photographer rather than cropping yourself out of a wedding photo. Here is what a good one delivers, what it is worth, and how to do it at scale. What you are actually paying for A genuine smile was the biggest single lift to how likable you read. A phone can capture a face. What it cannot do is control the variables that move perception, and those variables are measurable. Photo-rating platform PhotoFeeler ran the numbers on this. In a study built on more than 60,000 ratings of 800 business profile photos , the strongest factor for likability was a genuine smile with teeth visible, worth an average lift of 1.35 points on their scale. Formal dress drove the largest gains in perceived competence and influence, while sunglasses and shadowed eyes dragged scores down. A skilled photographer directs all of this live: the squint that reads as confidence instead of fear, the jawline, the lighting that keeps your eyes clear. That is the difference between a photographer who knows why a shot works and a friend hoping one of forty frames lands. Curious how your current photo reads on those same traits? Snappr's free Photo Analyzer scores it in seconds. As we covered in why your headshot is a key component of personal branding , the image is a deliberate business asset, not a formality. The cost of a bad one Skipping the professional route carries a price you pay later. Recruiters move fast. An eye-tracking study conducted by TheLadders found that recruiters spend roughly six seconds scanning a resume before deciding whether to keep reading, and online that snap judgment includes your photo. Employers are looking, too: a CareerBuilder survey found 70% of employers research candidates on social media, and 57% of them rejected someone based on what they found , with inappropriate photos the most common trigger. The photo is not decoration. It is evidence. Even the C-suite is not exempt. Snappr's look at the Fortune 500 CEOs with the best and worst headshots shows how many leaders still get the basics wrong. The upside runs the other way too. Snappr's own analysis found that professional headshots increase perceived trust and credibility by 78% . For a salesperson, a founder raising a round, or a consultant sending a proposal, that lift compounds across every first impression. When one headshot becomes fifty For an individual, booking a professional headshot photographer is a solved problem: find someone local, sit for an hour, get your files. The real challenge shows up at scale. A company that wants consistent headshots across a sales team, a leadership page, or a distributed workforce hits a different beast: sourcing photographers in every city, briefing each one so lighting and background match, chasing files, and re-shooting the person who joined last month. Do it ad hoc and your team page looks like a ransom note of mismatched styles. As we noted in why your startup's team photos can make or break your image , inconsistency reads as amateur even when each individual photo is fine. This is what Snappr was built to solve. You set your shoot guidelines once, and Snappr applies them to every session across a network covering 95% of the United States. You can book a vetted professional headshot photographer in about two minutes, on 24 hours' notice, and photos come back professionally edited within a day or two. One brief, one consistent look, whether it is one new hire or two hundred people across four offices. Snappr's business portraits service runs the coordination so your team does not have to. The takeaway A professional headshot photographer is not buying a nicer picture. It is buying control over a judgment that happens in a tenth of a second and repeats every time someone finds you online. For one person, that is worth an hour. For a team, it is worth a system. If you are standardizing headshots across a company, talk to Snappr's enterprise team about running your team's photography as one managed program. Frequently Asked Questions What does a professional headshot photographer do that I can't do myself? A professional headshot photographer controls lighting, angle, expression, and framing to shape how competent and trustworthy you appear. Research shows specific, controllable factors like a genuine smile and clear eyes measurably change how viewers rate a photo, and directing those in the moment is the skill you are paying for. How quickly do people judge a headshot? Almost instantly. Princeton research found that people form impressions of trustworthiness and competence from a face in about a tenth of a second, and extra viewing time only increases their confidence in that first read rather than changing it. Do professional headshots actually affect hiring and business outcomes? Yes. Recruiters scan a resume in roughly six seconds, and surveys show most employers research candidates online and reject some based on what they find, with inappropriate photos a leading cause. On the positive side, Snappr's analysis found professional headshots raise perceived trust and credibility by 78%. How do companies book a professional headshot photographer for a whole team? The reliable approach is to set shoot guidelines once and apply them to every session, rather than briefing a new photographer each time. Snappr does this across its network covering 95% of the US, so a distributed team gets one consistent look on one timeline instead of a patchwork of styles. Sources 1.
